0.comment: Ahpub: Ahpub and Ixquieh's Falling Out
0.content: The most detailed version comes from the Ring of Yaxche (2nd page). After Och-Kan became king and ordered fleeing dragons pursued, Ahpub marched on his sister's territory demanding the dragons they sheltered. After days facing each other he asked her to a private meeting, hoping sincere argument would bring her back to the vow. She called the king and her brother the real oathbreakers, said his vengeance had become blind bloodlust, and reminded him of Xbalanque's ban on harming peaceful Saurians. In a rage he put his sword to her neck merely to cow her, but struck her throat by accident and she bled out in his arms. He carried her into the incinerating fire. Both chiefs vanished; no war between tribes followed, though the king later demanded names of those who sheltered dragons.

1.comment: Ahpub: Competing Accounts of the Twins' End
1.content: Three accounts disagree. In the Ring of Yaxche, Ahpub's blade accidentally kills Ixquieh and he follows her into the fire. In the Flamelets text (5.8), Sundjatta says Ixquieh burned her workshop and writings and took her life while forcing her brother to do the same, to spare him the tarnished legacy of Och-Kan. Xona (5.5) says Ahpub, trusting Och-Kan after Xbalanque entered the Sacred Flame, led an army against the Children of Echoes; Ixquieh threw herself on his sword to force a shared death; but "legends claim" the siblings survived, saw through the plot to stir up discord and fled together to a distant land. No source resolves this.
